title: Sync hc JSON-RPC client spike
description: Spike a synchronous hc/herdr-core client matching this workspace's no-tokio convention (AGENTS.md: sync only, std UnixStream/threads/process stdio). Protocol facts already verified: 'hc connect --json' speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout (framed:false in hello unless negotiated); methods include hello, terminal.list/get/read/send/wait/keys/label, events.subscribe, machine.*; terminal.send returns {started,status,turn} and supports wait/if/force params; programs report Status{state: idle|working|done|blocked|error} via 7501 records; events stream as {"method":"event"} notifications — raw events.subscribe appeared to need the hello handshake first (unverified, check). Deliverable: minimal working probe (examples/ or a scratch bin, NOT wired into the router) that does hello + terminal.list + terminal.send + terminal.read + events.subscribe against the local core, plus notes on connection lifecycle/reconnect. Do not commit secrets; use throwaway terminals (terminal.run + terminal.rm).
close_reason: crates/hc-spike: sync HcClient over 'hc connect --json' stdio (process transport + id-mux reader thread + event fanout). Spike binary ALL PASS vs live hc 0.1.17: hello, terminal.list/run/send/read echo, events.subscribe notification, kill/rm cleanup. Key findings in docs/hc-migration/02-spike-notes.md: events.subscribe hijacks plain-mode connection (need 2nd connect for RPC), hello required before events, terminal.* param names, status.state model, machine/t7 addressing. Written by orchestrator after spawned agent produced corrupted output.
